definition: A function $F$ whose derivative is $f$, so $F'(x) = f(x)$; on an interval, any two antiderivatives of $f$ differ only by a constant.
The family of all antiderivatives of $f$, written $\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = F(x) + C$; for a power, $\int x^{n}\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$ only when $n \neq -1$.
The $+\,C$ at the end of an indefinite integral, there because any constant differentiates to $0$; a known point on the curve fixes its value.
A known pair of values, such as $y = 10$ when $x = 1$, substituted into the integrated function (not the derivative) to find the constant of integration.

The number $\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, found from $f$ between the limits $x = a$ and $x = b$; with $a < b$, it equals the area between the curve and the $x$-axis only when $f(x) \ge 0$ throughout, because parts below the axis count as negative.
